newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH to amortise DFS stake over 40 years.
newsitem.headline: LVMH to amortise DFS stake over 40 years.

text.p: LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault said on Thursday that the group would amortise its $2.6 billion acquisition of 61.25 percent of DFS over 40 years, and not over 25 to 30 years as previously envisaged.
He also told a news conference the strategy for DFS would not be affected by the suspension of talks to buy the remaining 38.75 percent stake held by DFS shareholder Robert Miller.
Miller said on Wednesday that LVMH had reneged on a February 3 agreement in principle to acquire his stake. He said he expected to take legal action.
Arnault said LVMH may eventually buy the stake.

"We will amortise goodwill longer than initially foreseen," he told the analysts' meeting. He said the acquisition would be amortised over 40 years. The group had initially planned to amortise it over 25 to 30 years.
A spokesman said the extension meant the goodwill amortisation would weigh less on annual results.
LVMH announced on Wednesday that talks with Miller had halted. Arnault said on Thursday that the negotiations had been "difficult".
"LVMH is the majority shareholder...and we didn't feel it was necessary to invest nine billion francs more," he said.
He reiterated that DFS would have a positive impact this year on LVMH's cashflow and pre-exceptional profit before goodwill amortisation and increase its operating profit by 30 percent.

The decision to suspend talks will have no effect on the development strategy for DFS, which he said was already in place. Its strategy is based on opening new outlets, at a pace of roughly 10 a year, and penetrate emerging Asian markets.

He said LVMH had seen the DFS management and was impressed. He said DFS would be run in a decentralised way as are all the brand businesses. "We think synergies, especially with Louis Vuitton, can go ahead," he said.

In an interview with Le Monde, Arnault said the talks with Miller were suspended but not broken off. "I don't rule out that we could buy his stake in the future, but it won't happen immediately," he was quoted as saying.
